text: Ken Skupski Jr., born on 9 April 1983 in Liverpool, is a British former professional tennis player who specialised in doubles. He achieved a career-high ATP doubles ranking of world No. 44 in July 2010 and won seven ATP Tour titles, most notably the 2021 Mexican Open with his younger brother Neal Skupski, with whom he regularly competed from 2013. Skupski is a three-time Grand Slam quarterfinalist, having reached the quarterfinals at the 2017 Wimbledon Championships in both men's and mixed doubles, and at the 2020 Australian Open in men's doubles. At the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi, he won a silver medal in men's doubles with Ross Hutchins and a bronze in mixed doubles with Sarah Borwell. He also represented Great Britain in the Davis Cup on two occasions in 2010. His father, Ken Sr., is a retired police officer of Polish descent, and his mother, Mary, is a golfer. Skupski is a devoted fan of Liverpool Football Club and a keen golfer with a handicap of six. As youngsters, the brothers lost a doubles match against a pairing with special educational and emotional needs, an experience they say motivated them to train harder and contributed to their future success. Skupski graduated from Louisiana State University in May 2007, where he was a NCAA Doubles finalist in 2005, a two-time Southeastern Conference Coaches Indoor Champion (the only player in the conference history to win back-to-back titles), fourth in the school's history for total wins with 107, and a six-time All-American (two in singles, one in doubles, three in academic categories). In June 2009, he and Colin Fleming defeated the world no. 1 doubles pair, Mike Bryan and Bob Bryan, at the Queen's Club tournament. However, he was eliminated in the first round at Wimbledon for the second consecutive year, again partnering Fleming, and lost in the mixed doubles second round. In September 2009, he was part of the Great Britain Davis Cup squad for the Europe/Africa Zone Group 1 relegation play-off against Poland, acting as cover and helping prepare for Poland's top-10 doubles team, but did not play; Great Britain lost 3–2 and were relegated to Group II. In September 2009, he won the Open de Moselle in France with Fleming, defeating Arnaud Clément and Michaël Llodra 2–6, 6–4, 10–5, and two months later won the St Petersburg Open, defeating Jérémy Chardy and Richard Gasquet 2–6, 7–5, 10–4. At the 2010 Australian Open, he and Fleming reached the second round before losing to Michael Kohlmann and Jarkko Nieminen 6–3, 4–6, 3–6; at the French Open, they lost in the second round to Wesley Moodie and Dick Norman 6–7(5–7), 6–4, 6–7(4–7). In June 2010, he reached the Eastbourne Open final, losing to Mariusz Fyrstenberg and Marcin Matkowski in three sets with Fleming; he finally won a match at Wimbledon in the first round, but lost in the second to the Bryan brothers in straight sets with Fleming. He competed at all four Grand Slams in the same year for the first time, but lost in the first round at the US Open in straight sets with Fleming. In July 2010, he and Fleming played in the Davis Cup tie against Turkey at Eastbourne, securing a 6–3, 6–4, 6–4 win that gave Great Britain a 3–0 lead, ending a five-match losing streak and marking their first Davis Cup win in three years. In October 2010, at the Commonwealth Games in Delhi, Skupski and Hutchins won the men's doubles silver medal, losing to Paul Hanley and Peter Luczak in the final, and later won the mixed doubles bronze medal by defeating Ross Hutchins and Anna Smith with Sarah Borwell, who had never played together before and were brought together by their shared coach, Louis Cayer. After a poor run of results, Skupski and Fleming ended their partnership in early 2011, with their final tournament being St. Petersburg, where they lost in the first round. In January 2011, he lost in the first round at the Australian Open with Travis Parrott in straight sets; in February, he partnered Robin Haase at the Marseille Open, reaching the final and winning the title by defeating Julien Benneteau and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga 6–3, 6–7(4–7), [13–11], marking his first title in over a year and a half. At the French Open, he lost in the first round to Fleming 4–6, 4–6 with Igor Zelenay; at Wimbledon, he lost in the first round with Robin Haase; in mixed doubles, he partnered Elena Baltacha and reached the second round before losing to Andy Ram and Meghann Shaughnessy 4–6, 4–6. At the Australian Open in January, he lost in the first round with Xavier Malisse in straight sets, marking his fifth consecutive first-round exit without winning a set. In mid-June, he reached the final of the Aegon International with Jamie Delgado, losing to Colin Fleming and Ross Hutchins 4–6, 3–6, his first final in over a year. At Wimbledon, he broke his Grand Slam curse by reaching the second round after winning a grueling five-set first-round match with Delgado, but lost in straight sets 6–7(2–7), 0–6, 2–6 to the Bryan brothers. In mixed doubles with Melanie South, they reached the third round before losing to Nenad Zimonjić and Katarina Srebotnik 4–6, 7–6(7–5), 7–9. A month later, he and Delgado reached their second final of the season at the Farmers Classic, losing to Ruben Bemelmans and Xavier Malisse 6–7(5–7), 6–4, [10–7]. At the US Open, he and Delgado reached the third round before losing to Marcel Granollers and Marc López in straight sets 2–6, 4–6, having defeated Jürgen Melzer and Philipp Petzschner in the second round in straight sets. Initially partnering with Delgado, Skupski increasingly played with his brother Neal from 2013 due to Neal's lower ranking, winning six Challenger titles and reaching the final at the Kremlin Cup. As their partnership did not qualify them for the French Open, they split; Ken partnered New Zealander Michael Venus, a fellow LSU alumnus, and Neal teamed with American Bradley Klahn, both losing in the first round. In July 2013, Neal was playing in World Team Tennis in the US, so Skupski partnered Divij Sharan, winning the doubles title at the Euro 42,500 men's Challenger in Recanati, Italy, defeating Ilija Bozoljac and Flavio Cipolla 4–6, 7–6(3), 10–6. In September, the Skupskis won the St. Remy Challenger in France, playing only two matches due to byes and a semi-final walkover, defeating Andrej Martin and Igor Zelenay 6–4, 6–1 as top seeds. At the 2017 Wimbledon Championships, Skupski reached the quarterfinals as a wildcard with his brother Neal, losing to the 4th seeded pair Łukasz Kubot and Marcelo Melo, and also reached the mixed doubles quarterfinals with Jocelyn Rae. The Skupski brothers won their first ATP title together at the Open Sud de France. At the 2020 Australian Open, Skupski reached the quarterfinals partnering Santiago González for the first time at a Major and second overall. In March 2021, he won his sixth ATP title and first at the ATP 500 level with Neal at the Mexican Open. In June 2021, he won the Nottingham Open on grass partnering Matt Reid. At the end of the year, he won his second ATP title of the season, the 2021 Sofia Open, partnering Jonny O'Mara. In June, partnering Jonny O'Mara, he defended his Nottingham Open title by defeating Julian Cash and Henry Patten in the final after saving three championship points. Skupski announced that Wimbledon 2022 would be his last professional tournament; partnering Jonny O'Mara again, he won the first round against Julio Peralta and Alejandro Tabilo, and the second round against Marcelo Melo and Raven Klaasen, but lost in the round of 16 to 11th seeds Andreas Mies and Kevin Krawietz, which was his final match. He was scheduled to play in the mixed doubles event with Heather Watson, but she withdrew before their first-round match due to a knee injury. Skupski played two seasons in World Team Tennis, debuting in 2017 with the Orange County Breakers and being named WTT's Male Rookie of the Year, and joining the expansion Orlando Storm in 2019 for their inaugural season. He rejoined the Orlando Storm in 2020, beginning on 12 July, marking his second time with the team. During the season, he partnered Tennys Sandgren in men's doubles and Jessica Pegula in mixed doubles, earning a season-high 56% of games won in men's doubles, helping the Storm secure a No. 3 seed in the WTT Playoffs, though they ultimately lost to the Chicago Smash in the semifinals.
